correctness.rationale: Direct realized-group payoff subtraction proves the exact Bernstein gain coefficients. The first coefficients through quorum minus one increase strictly and the later block does not decrease; Descartes then gives at most three positive roots counting multiplicity. A sign-pattern argument allows at most one asymptotically stable mixed edge root. At N=4 the exact rational parameter set yields gain polynomial (4864 z^3 - 8592 z^2 + 4512 z - 659)/2500 with four alternating exact rational signs and three disjoint rational root brackets. The edge and transverse eigenvalue signs imply saddle/sink/source and both pure corners sink; every relevant eigenvalue is strictly nonzero. Embedded exact-arithmetic replay tests independently verify conditional payoff subtraction, coefficients, brackets and stability signs. The all-N claim is an analytic proof, not a finite computational inference. No full-simplex global dynamics are claimed.

value.rationale: Li et al. use numerical branch continuation and obtain two mixed edge states, leaving an identifiable nontrivial question about maximum multiplicity under the coupled quorum, loss and exponential-risk restrictions. The all-group-size 3-root bound is sharp at the smallest feasible group; explicit exact parameters produce the extra hyperbolic source, while a separate sign-pattern argument proves that no more than one mixed edge state is attracting along the edge. This separates equilibrium complexity from attracting behavioral states and supplies a reproducible exact test case. The result does not claim policy optimization or empirical applicability.
